Asset batches, contact sheets, seamless panoramas and background removal.

- **`codex-img batch <spec.json>`** builds a set of assets from one JSON spec: it generates each missing raw image (references first, several at a time), then converts every raw image, rewriting only files whose bytes changed. A shared style, defaults and per-asset options; the whole spec is validated before anything runs.
- **`codex-img sheet`** lays images out in one labelled grid on a common baseline, to review a batch at a glance.
- **`codex-img tile`** makes a panorama wrap around seamlessly: it repaints only a band around the seam and keeps every other pixel. One image of quota.
- **`--key`** removes a painted-in background (sea under a boat, sky behind a building) by flood fill from the edges. `--key-region`, `--key-spread` and `--key-cut` control where and how far, and `--trim-density` keeps leftover specks from becoming a sprite's edge.
- **`convert --force`** replaces outputs and leaves files that already hold the same bytes untouched.
- **`-c` is deterministic:** the same input and options now give the same bytes every time.
- Batches refuse to convert over their own raw images, and the Python fallback refuses `sheet`, `batch` and `tile` instead of treating them as prompts.
